result.response:
For a small nonprofit looking to avoid steep monthly per-subscriber fees (like Mailchimp or Constant Contact), self-hosting a newsletter platform is a cost-effective alternative.

When self-hosting, the setup typically requires two components:
1. **The Newsletter Management Software** (the self-hosted app that manages lists, drafts, and campaigns).
2. **An SMTP Relay Service** (the outbound mail infrastructure to ensure emails actually reach inboxes instead of spam folders).

---

### 1. Top Self-Hosted Newsletter Software

#### **[Listmonk](https://listmonk.app/) (Best Overall / High Performance)**
* **License:** Free, Open Source (AGPL-3.0)
* **Stack:** Go + PostgreSQL (available as a single binary or lightweight Docker image)
* **Why it fits nonprofits:**
  * Extremely low resource footprint; can comfortably run on a minimal $4–$5/month VPS.
  * Handles millions of subscribers and emails with zero bloat.
  * Includes list segmentation, multi-language templating, transactional email support, and clean analytics.
  * Connects to any standard SMTP provider.

#### **[Ghost](https://ghost.org/) (Best for Integrated Blog + Newsletter)**
* **License:** Open Source (MIT)
* **Stack:** Node.js + MySQL
* **Why it fits nonprofits:**
  * Ideal if the nonprofit needs both a public-facing website/blog and an email newsletter in one platform.
  * Offers clean publishing, membership management, and public archives of past newsletters.
  * *Note:* Self-hosted Ghost requires configuration with [Mailgun](https://www.mailgun.com/) for bulk newsletter delivery.

#### **[Keila](https://www.keila.io/) (Best for Simplicity & Privacy)**
* **License:** Open Source (AGPL-3.0)
* **Stack:** Elixir / Phoenix + PostgreSQL
* **Why it fits nonprofits:**
  * Built as a modern, GDPR-compliant alternative to Mailchimp.
  * Clean, minimal user interface that non-technical staff or volunteers can easily navigate.
  * Supports custom form builders, segmenting, and Markdown/block-based email editors.

#### **[Sendy](https://sendy.co/) (Best Non-Technical, One-Time Purchase)**
* **License:** Proprietary (One-time license fee: ~$69)
* **Stack:** PHP + MySQL (runs on standard shared web hosting cPanel or a VPS)
* **Why it fits nonprofits:**
  * Very easy to install for organizations already using standard PHP/cPanel web hosting.
  * Built specifically to plug into **Amazon SES** for near-zero sending costs.
  * Simple, non-developer-friendly dashboard for campaign drafting, list maintenance, and bounce handling.

#### **[Mautic](https://www.mautic.org/) (Best for Full Marketing Automation & CRM)**
* **License:** Open Source (GPL-3.0)
* **Stack:** PHP + MySQL
* **Why it fits nonprofits:**
  * Suitable if the nonprofit needs advanced donor journeys, drip campaigns, lead scoring, and CRM capabilities.
  * *Trade-off:* Significantly higher server resource requirements (2GB–4GB+ RAM) and steeper learning curve compared to Listmonk or Keila.

---

### 2. Critical Partner: Outbound SMTP Relays

A common pitfall in self-hosting is attempting to send bulk email directly from a VPS IP address. Mail providers (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo) will likely flag or drop these emails. A self-hosted tool should be paired with a reputable email relay:

* **[Amazon SES (Simple Email Service)](https://aws.amazon.com/ses/):** The most cost-effective solution ($0.10 per 1,000 emails sent).
* **[Brevo (formerly Sendinblue)](https://www.brevo.com/):** Free tier available (up to 300 emails/day), with nonprofit discounts on paid tiers.
* **[Mailgun](https://www.mailgun.com/) or [Postmark](https://postmarkapp.com/):** High deliverability and developer-friendly setup (Postmark offers a 20% nonprofit discount).

---

### Recommendation for a Small Nonprofit

* **If technical help is minimal and you want a simple, budget-friendly setup:** Choose **Sendy + Amazon SES** (can run on existing web hosting).
* **If you have someone comfortable with Docker or basic server management:** Choose **Listmonk + Amazon SES** (free, extremely low-cost hosting, modern feature set).
* **If you want your website content and email publication combined:** Choose **Ghost**.
* **Essential Setup Step:** Ensure you configure **DKIM, SPF, and DMARC** DNS records for your sending domain to meet modern inbox deliverability requirements.
